ess:leave:overview.title: ESS → Leave → Overview
ess:leave:overview.what: The employee’s leave home: balances at a glance, recent leave activity, upcoming leave and the next public holiday. Also where they start a leave or comp off request.
sections: Design notes

Field explanations, panel descriptions, worked examples and policy notes on this page are tooltips (info icon next to the label or title), not visible text. Keep only values, choices, statuses and errors always visible.
What’s on the page
Sub-tabs: Overview · My requests (count of open) · Public holidays. Top right: "Request comp off" (when on) · "Request LOP" · "Apply for leave" (primary).
Banners when they apply: on probation; leaving date set (settlement per each type’s leaving rule).

One card grid: a card per yearly leave type (name, "available / total days", View details) and a grey info card per per-event type ("Up to 7 days per event · Working days · apply when needed") on the left, and two side cards always in the right-hand column: "Upcoming leave" (only the next leave the employee applied for that hasn’t ended, whatever its status: pending, approved, update requested or rejected; not withdrawn or cancelled; with its status pill and See all requests) and "Next public holiday" (name, date, "in N days", See all holidays).

Layout by number of leave cards: 1–2 → one row (leave cards, then the two side cards at the right end); 3–4 → 3 columns: leave cards in a 2×2 block on the left, side cards stacked in the right column; 5–6 → 4 columns: leave cards 3×2 on the left, side cards stacked on the right; 7+ → same, leave cards continue in more rows. Phones: 2 columns, side cards after the leave cards. Cards in a row are the same height.
Recent activity below the grid: last 10 changes, newest first; leave rows open the request drawer.
Rules
Types shown = active leave types whose "Applies to" matches the employee (all / female / male). Comp off appears only when comp off is on.
Available = credited so far − approved leave − late check-in deductions − leave still in request (pending or update requested). Example: 10 credited, 4 taken, 2 requested = 4 available.
Total = this leave cycle’s entitlement (pro-rated for joiners/leavers) + carried forward. Comp off total = earned and not expired.

Recent activity sources: leave / comp off / cancellation / change requests (with their latest action), credits (start of cycle, monthly, daily, carry forward), late deductions (and "dispute pending"), reversals, comp off expiries. Sorted by the date of the change, not the leave date.
Apply for leave (modal, opened from the button)

Fields: Leave type → the available balance appears immediately ("7 days available of 17 this year", plus "2 days waiting for approval are already taken off"); Full days / Half days; From; To; Which half (half days only, applies to every working day in the range); Supporting document (only when the type’s rule needs it for that duration); Reason.
Duration line: working days only (employee’s own schedule; weekly offs and public holidays not counted). Half days = 0.5 per working day. With the sandwich rule on: "+ N days off in between".

Refuse with a clear message: end before start; no working days; dates overlapping existing leave (approved, pending or update requested); not enough available; type "not available" during probation; document missing when required; no reason.
Sends a leave request into the approval chain (leave approvers from settings). Footer line names the approvers.
Calendar-day types count every day in the range ("12 calendar days, weekends and public holidays included").
Footer note: "Need unpaid leave (loss of pay)? That’s only once all your paid leave is used. Email Admin / HR to arrange it."

Per-event types: the Duration (full/half) choice is hidden. Fields: the event date (label from the trigger, e.g. "Date of birth or adoption"); Start date (only dates inside the window can be picked; disabled until the event date is set); End date fills in automatically for the full entitlement (working or calendar days per the type), can be shortened but not extended; hint "Can start between … and …. …taken in one go"; the supporting document field with HR’s wording when required. Refused: no event date, start outside the window, longer than the entitlement, or a second request for the same event ("It has to be taken in one go; change that request instead").

Maternity in the form: "Which child is this?" First child / Second child / Third child or later ("This sets your entitlement. HR checks it when they approve."). It sets the number of days and the earliest start (up to the before-weeks, 6 for the third child or later); the latest start is the after-weeks. Event date label: "Expected or actual date of delivery".
Half days are offered only for leave types that allow them (per-type setting).
Request LOP (modal)

Loss of pay is the only unpaid leave. Same form as a regular leave without the type: Full / Half days, From, To, Which half, Reason. Working days only. Box: "Unpaid leave · these days are deducted from your salary".

Setting (Leave → Configuration → Loss of pay): "Only once paid leave is used up" (default) or "Any time". With the default, if any yearly balance (incl. comp off; per-event types don’t count) is above 0, the modal shows "You still have paid leave: 9.5 Annual · 6.5 Casual…" and Send is disabled.

Creates a leave request with leaveType "Loss of pay" (lop = true): same approvers, same overlap check, no balance and no limit. Approvers see "Unpaid: payroll treats these days as loss of pay." instead of a balance line. In the drawer: Withdraw / Cancel only (no Edit or Change). Attendance and timesheet show the days as leave; payroll/LOP (owned by another team) reads them as loss of pay.
Request comp off (modal)

Day picker is a calendar: only weekly offs and public holidays can be selected (working days are disabled; extra hours on a working day are overtime). Also disabled: future days, days older than the expiry window, days already claimed. Days the employee worked are marked with a dot.
Legend: Public holiday · Weekly off · You worked · Not available.
Hours come from attendance (or timesheet in timesheet-only mode). Half a shift or more = 0.5 day, full shift = 1 day. Refused if the day was claimed as overtime.
Data the page needs
Balances per type: available, total, credited, approved, in request, carried forward.
Activity feed (last 10, newest change first). Upcoming leave. Holidays for the year. Employee status (probation) and leaving date.
Email notifications

When a leave application reaches an approval level, the approver(s) at that level get an email. Full rules in "How to use these notes" → Shared rules → "Email notifications for leave applications". Email wording comes from product separately.

ess:leave:requests.title: ESS → Leave → My requests
ess:leave:requests.what: Every leave-related request the employee has raised, and the place to view, edit, change, cancel or withdraw them.
sections: What’s on the page
Status filter: All · In progress · Approved · Rejected / withdrawn (with counts).

Table: Leave type · Start date · End date · Duration (with half-day info) · Status · Action (View). Comp off, cancellation and change requests are listed too ("Comp off (earned)", "Cancel Annual", "Change Annual"). A pending cancellation or change of a leave shows under its status.
Clicking a row (or View) opens a right-side drawer.
The drawer

Details: type, from, to, day type (full / first half / second half, "of each day" for ranges), duration, reason, document; for change requests also "Was: …". For comp off: day worked, hours, comp off days.
Banners: the approver’s comment when an update was requested; "A cancellation/change of this leave is waiting for {approver}".
Approval chain, then History (every action with who, when and comment).

Actions by state: Pending → Edit request, Withdraw. Update requested → Update and resubmit, Withdraw. Approved → Change leave (if not finished), Cancel leave. Rejected / withdrawn / cancelled → read only.
Withdraw asks for confirmation ("Withdraw this request?").
Editing and changing
Editing a pending request updates it in place and sends it back to the start of the approval chain (Level 1).

Changing APPROVED leave creates a "leave change" request (new type/dates/half/reason) that goes through the leave approvers. The original leave stays exactly as it is until the change is approved; then it is replaced. Balance check allows the original days back if it’s the same type.
Same validations as Apply (overlap with other leave, balance, working days, sandwich rule).
Cancelling and past dates

Cancel leave asks for "Cancel from" (whole leave, or from a later date) and a reason, then goes for approval. The leave stays booked until approved; then the days return to the balance and attendance / timesheet update.

Past dates: the employee may cancel or shorten approved leave in the past ONLY for days they actually worked: a check-in on each past working day being removed (attendance modes), or timesheet entries (timesheet-only). Otherwise refuse: "Past leave can only be cancelled for days you actually worked. There’s no check-in on Mon 9 Nov. Raise an attendance correction for those days first."
HR cancelling from Payroll is not limited by this rule and applies immediately.
Data / API
List the employee’s leave, comp off, cancellation and change requests with status and trail. Endpoints to edit a pending request, create change/cancel requests, withdraw.

sections: Design notes

Field explanations, panel descriptions, worked examples and policy notes on this page are tooltips (info icon next to the label or title), not visible text. Keep only values, choices, statuses and errors always visible.
What’s on the page
Scope: everything here is per leave type. Company-wide rules (credit date, rounding, leave year, sandwich rule, LOP, comp off) are in Configuration.

Table columns only: Leave type (with a small line: Yearly balance / Per event / Statutory · required or optional / Inactive) · Number of days ("12 days a year", "7 days per event", "182 days per birth") · Accrual type and rate ("Monthly · 1 day a month", "Per event") · Leave balance carryover ("Yes, up to 30 days" / "No") · Applicable gender · Action (View, Edit, Delete).
View shows every rule of the type, grouped as in the drawer. Delete is disabled for used types and for Maternity.

Maternity is set up for every company and can’t be deleted or renamed. Required when the company has more than 10 current employees (headcount from Employees, people without a past leaving date): always on, switch locked. 10 or fewer: optional, off by default.
Delete asks for confirmation ("Delete Paternity?" … can’t be undone; disable instead if you might use it again).
Drawer: every type
Name; Kind: Yearly balance / Per event; Count leave in: Working days / Calendar days; Applicable gender. Maternity skips kind, count and gender (fixed: per event, calendar days, female).

Footer (existing types only): "Disable leave type" (red outline, left) / "Enable leave type" when disabled, plus Cancel and Save. It applies straight away: disabling hides the type from employees without deleting it; balances and past leave stay. Tooltip explains this. For Maternity the button is disabled while it’s legally required (more than 10 employees); with 10 or fewer it switches maternity on/off. Disabled types show "Inactive" in the table.
Drawer: Yearly balance (three phases)
Days per year (shows the monthly amount).

1 · During probation (new joiners): "Can employees on probation use it?" Yes / No. If yes, "How it’s credited during probation": Monthly / Daily / All at once. If no, nothing is credited until HR marks the employee Active. Stored as prob = none / monthly / daily / full.

2 · After probation (regular employees): "How it’s credited": All at once / Monthly / Daily. "At the end of the leave cycle", four options: All lapse · All encashed · Carry forward (up to the limit; days above it lapse) · Carry forward, encash the rest (up to the limit moves on; days above it are paid out). The two carry options show "Carry forward up to N days". Stored as yearEnd lapse / encash / carry + excess lapse / encash. Runs automatically on the last working day of the cycle.
3 · When an employee leaves: pro-rated to the last working day, then Unused leave: Encash / Bring last working day forward / Lapse (store the rule; F&F is a later module).
Requests: Half days (on/off, per type; the Apply form only offers half days for types that allow it); Supporting documents (on/off; when on, "for leave longer than N days", 0 = every request).
Drawer: Maternity (statutory per-event type)
Banner: statutory, numbers follow the Code on Social Security, 2020; more generous than the law is allowed, less is not.
Offer maternity leave (headcount rule above). Triggered by: Expected or actual date of delivery (fixed).
Days of leave by child: First child, Second child, Third child or later, each a number of days with the legal minimum shown (182 / 182 / 84). Saving below the minimum is refused.

When the leave can start: "From N weeks before the delivery date to M weeks after it" (defaults 8 and 0). The law caps "before" at 8 weeks (6 for the third child or later, applied automatically). All the days run on from the start date in one go. A worked example under the fields updates live (due date 1 December).
Supporting documents: on by default, plus what to ask for.
Drawer: other per-event types

Triggered by (Childbirth or adoption / Childbirth / Adoption / Miscarriage or medical termination / Surgery or medical procedure / Other event); Number of days (days or weeks, for one event, in one go); When the leave can start (N days before to M days after the event, empty = no limit, with a live example); Supporting documents (on/off + what to ask for).

pay:settings:leave:config.title: Payroll settings → Leave → Configuration
sections: Design notes

Field explanations, panel descriptions, worked examples and policy notes on this page are tooltips (info icon next to the label or title), not visible text. Keep only values, choices, statuses and errors always visible.

Negative balance: on/off; "Up to N days below zero per leave type" (empty = no limit). When on, employees (and HR) can book more than the available balance up to that limit; the balance goes negative and is recovered from the next credits, or in the full & final settlement if they leave. Yearly balance types only. Approvers see "−1.5 after this (negative balance, recovered from the next credits)".
Panels
Scope: these rules apply to every leave type (note at the top of the page). Rules for one leave type are set on that type in Leave types.

Credit date: Start / End / Custom, applied to both monthly and daily credits (types credited all at once aren’t affected). Start: monthly on the 1st for the month ahead; daily at the start of each day. End: monthly on the last day once the month is worked; daily once the day is over. Custom: monthly on a set day (1–28); daily from a set time (default 12:00 PM). Two small cards under the choice spell out what it means for monthly and for daily credits. Joiners follow the same schedule from their joining date.
Rounding: No rounding / Nearest half day / Nearest day. Applied to credited-so-far and the year’s total (e.g. 14 a year = 1.167 a month).
Leave year: company cycle (start day + month) or each employee’s joining date. Balances roll forward automatically on the last working day of the cycle, following each type’s year-end rule.

Loss of pay (unpaid leave): "Only once paid leave is used up" / "Any time, even with paid leave left". "Used up" = all yearly balances (and comp off) at 0; per-event leave doesn’t count. LOP has no limit and follows the leave approvers.
Comp off: on/off + expires after N days.
Half-day leave is no longer here: it’s a per-type setting in the leave type drawer.

Sandwich rule: on/off. When on, "When it applies": Always / Only for longer leave ("when a request covers more than N days in total, from the first to the last day"); "What counts as leave": Weekly offs, Public holidays (checkboxes). Only days off between the first and last working day of the request count. A worked example updates live: leave 1st–9th with the 6th and 7th weekly offs and the 4th a holiday = 6 days without the rule, 9 with it (if the request is longer than the threshold).
Not settings (fixed rules, documented in the leave engine, not shown here)
Probation: employees on Probation follow each leave type’s probation rule until HR marks them Active (Payroll → Leave → Balances). There is no probation length to set.
Pro-rating: a month counts if someone joins on or before the 15th, or leaves on or after the 15th. Credits aren’t rounded.
Late check-in deduction is an Attendance setting (Payroll settings → Attendance, timesheet & overtime), not a Leave one.

sections: Rules
Level 1 and Level 2 each offer: Reporting manager · Admin / HR (decided in that service in Payroll) · a specific person (managers and the CEO). Level 2 also has None (level 1 is final).
Typical setup: Reporting manager → Admin / HR. The manager approves first, then it comes to Payroll → Leave → Requests for the final approval.
"Reporting manager" at Level 2 resolves to the employee’s manager when Level 1 approves; if that’s the same person who approved Level 1, the request is final.

Approvers are fixed on each request when it’s submitted, so changing this doesn’t move requests in flight. Leave cancellations, changes and comp off use the same approvers. Older team values (Payroll, HR, Admin, Finance) all show as Admin / HR.

Extra approval for longer leave (on/off): when a request is longer than N days, an endorsement step is added after Level 1 and before Level 2. Endorser: Department head of the employee’s department, or a specific person. Skipped if the endorser is the Level 1 approver or the employee. Shown in the approval chain as "{name} (endorsement)"; the item waits in that person’s My team → Approvals. Applies to leave and leave changes.
Email notifications

When a leave application reaches an approval level, the approver(s) at that level get an email. Full rules in "How to use these notes" → Shared rules → "Email notifications for leave applications". Email wording comes from product separately.

ess:time:attendance.what: Check in/out, breaks, the month and corrections. (Attendance is the next module after Leave.)
sections: Attendance rules
One check-in and one check-out per day. No automatic check-out: a session stays open until the employee checks out, even across days.
Overnight work counts to the check-in day: store outDays (0 = same day, 1 = next day…). Hours worked = check-out + outDays × 24h − check-in, breaks included.

Breaks: multiple per day, { start, end, description }. Start/End only while checked in; checking out ends a running break. Today’s breaks can be edited directly (no overlaps, inside the session); past breaks only via a correction.
Late mark: check-in after shift start + grace. With first-half leave, the shift start moves to mid-shift. No exceptions for working late the night before.
Location (attendance-only mode): optional day-level timeline [{ at, location, client }], changeable any time; first entry from the pre-check-in choice.
Late check-in deduction
Each late mark deducts settings.lateDays (default 0.5, 0 = off) immediately, from the order set in Leave settings (default Annual, then Casual, then loss of pay).
It stays deducted while a dispute (correction) is pending. When the correction is approved and the day is no longer late, it’s reversed automatically and shown as "+0.5 reversed".
Attendance tab Notes panel (latest 5): no dispute yet → Raise dispute; pending → waiting for {approver}; rejected → shows who and their comment, with Dispute again.

Header: one "Request correction" button. Grid: Today | Month totals (3×3) | My correction requests (spans both rows, same height as the left side, scrolls inside). Calendar spans the first two columns.
Totals: Present, Late, Half day, Absent, On leave, Holidays, Worked off-days, Break time, and "Xh worked, Yh overtime".

Correction popup: date picker, "Recorded now", check-in, check-out, same day / next day, reason. Refuses future dates and days with a pending correction. Asks before replacing edited times when the date changes.

sections: Timesheet entries
Entry: { id, date, start|null, end|null, startNext, endNext, mins, description, project|null, location, client|null }. Hours-only entries allowed (parse 1:30, 1.5, 1h 30m).
An end earlier than the start means the next morning ("Ends next day"). On an overnight day, a start before check-in means after midnight.
Overlaps are blocked, including against breaks and leave/holiday rows.
Location per entry (attendance + timesheet and timesheet-only): Office / Home / Client site (+ client name, required). Defaults to the last used.
Project codes when HR turns them on: required on every entry.
Rows the system adds (read-only, not stored as entries)
Breaks (description editable), approved leave (full shift, or the half for half days), weekday public holidays (skipped if the employee checked in that day).
They count towards logged hours, never count as overtime, and never make a period "Saved" or need submitting.
Targets and saving
Day target = hours worked (full check-in to check-out). Timesheet-only = shift length. Leave or public holiday (no check-in) = shift length. Half-day leave = worked + half shift.
Every change saves immediately; changed dates are tracked (dirty set) and shown as "Saved" until submitted.

Submit (view bar) sends every period overlapping the current Day/Week/Month view that is Draft or Update requested. If only edits of already-sent periods are included: "Only your changes will be resubmitted" + the changed dates. Day view notes that the whole filing period goes.
Auto-submit at the HR-set day and time sends Draft periods with entries (and their attendance). Anything already sent is left alone.
Editing a period after it was sent (even approved) moves it back to Draft with a baseline; reviewers see "What changed".
Period statuses: draft → submitted (with Level 1) → with_payroll (with Level 2) → approved; rejected = Update requested.
Timesheet screen
Calendar 65% / Notices 35% (same height, scrolls inside). Legend: Saved · Submitted · Update requested · Leave · Public holiday · Selected (red outline on the days in view).
Notices: the focused week’s status, "Needs your action" across all weeks with Go to day, Unlogged hours, History. No Submit in Notices.
Single bar per day (no second meter). The axis stretches past midnight on overnight days.

intro: These notes follow you: open any page in the prototype, click "Developer notes", and you see what that page is, everything on it, its rules and the data it needs. Move to another page (or sub-tab) and the notes switch with you.

At the bottom of every page’s notes is "Build it with Claude": a ready prompt for Claude Code that builds that page in the real code base. Copy it, paste it in, and it will read these notes and the prototype.

We’re building ESS module by module: Leave first, then Attendance, then Timesheet, then Overtime, Reimbursements and Profile. Leave pages have the most detail. Other pages have notes too, but build them when their module comes up.
read: The prototype has three areas in the left sidebar: ESS - Employee (an employee, Rohan Mehta), ESS - Manager (a manager and approver, Priya Nair) and Payroll (the admin/HR side, opened from the Payroll dashboard’s Quick actions).

Demo controls (bottom right) change the scenario: tracking mode, employee dates and status, payroll processing, resetting data. They’re for demos only and must not ship. Developer notes are prototype-only too.
Data in the prototype is fake and stored in your browser. The rules (balances, accruals, approvals) are real: build them the same way, as tested functions on the backend or the shared rules layer.
When the notes and the prototype disagree, the notes win. If something isn’t covered, copy how the prototype behaves and write the decision down.

Design: follow the Peko One design system (Figma: Peko One - Design System) on top of the Payroll antd theme. Primary #FF4F4F (tints #FFF2F2 / #FFE7E7 / #FFD6D6), neutral slate greys (#F8FAFC → #0F172A), success #43B75D, warning #F59E0B, error #EF4444; Roboto; headings 20/18/16 semibold, body 14, hints and tags 12. Buttons: primary solid red, secondary red outline, neutral grey outline, tertiary red text. Inputs: #E2E8F0 border, 8px radius, red focus ring. Page sections use underline tabs; filters use the compact segmented control.

Help text: only core information is always on screen. Explanations, rules and examples go in a tooltip: a 13px grey info icon (antd InfoCircleOutlined, #8993A4) next to the field label, panel title or button, showing an antd Tooltip on hover or focus. This is the same pattern the Payroll code already uses (e.g. "Rollout Salary").
order: Leave module, in this order: Payroll settings → Leave (Leave types, Public holidays, Configuration, Approvals) → the leave rules (balances, accruals, probation, carry forward, sandwich, comp off) → ESS Leave (Overview, Apply, Leave type details, My requests + drawer, Public holidays) → approver views (My team Approvals and Leave calendar) → Payroll Leave (Overview, Leaves, Requests, Balances, Add leave) → links to Attendance and Timesheet (late deductions, leave rows).
Settings come first because they decide how every other Leave screen behaves.
shared: How to read the prototype

All business rules are plain functions in the prototype file (attOf, workedMins, dayStatus, expectedFor, otSuggestion, leaveYear, leaveBalances, leaveDayCount, l1For / l2For, personQueue, submitWeek, decideRequest, applyEffects). Port them as tested rules (src/prototype/rules or the backend). Screens should call the rules, never re-derive them.

Demo personas: ESS - Employee = Rohan Mehta (ACME-002), ESS - Manager = Priya Nair. 21 employees, ACME-001 to ACME-021; ACME-021 (CEO) has no manager. Demo data is rebuilt each week and stored in localStorage.
Times are shown in 12-hour format everywhere (9:30 AM). Inputs stay as time pickers. Dates as "Tue 13 Oct".
The "Demo controls" and "Developer notes" buttons are prototype-only. Do not ship them.
Tracking modes
Company setting: attendance only / timesheet only / attendance + timesheet / neither.
Use two helpers everywhere: attOn = attendance or both; tsOn = timesheet or both. Never write "not timesheet means attendance", because "neither" breaks it.
Neither: no attendance or timesheet UI at all (cards, recent days table, tabs, calendars). Leave, overtime and reimbursements still work.
Approval engine (all request types)

Per function (attendance corrections, timesheets, overtime, leave, reimbursements) HR sets Level 1 and Level 2. Each can be: Reporting manager, Admin / HR (decided in Payroll), or a specific person. Level 2 can also be None (level 1 is final).
Resolve the approvers when the item is submitted (and Level 2 again when Level 1 approves) and store them on the item. Changing settings later must not move items already in flight.
No manager (CEO) or "Reporting manager" pointing at themselves: Level 1 is skipped.

Actions at either level: Approve, Ask for update (comment required, goes straight back to the employee, status update_requested; resubmitting starts again at Level 1), Reject (requests only). Level 2 approval is final and runs the effects (attendance updated, leave applied, deduction reversed, etc).

Queues: items waiting on a person appear in that person’s My team → Approvals. Items waiting on a team appear in Payroll → {service} → Requests. Payroll can see items sitting with people (read-only) and send a Remind notification.
Leave cancellation and comp off requests use the leave approvers. Profile updates go straight to HR (no manager).
Request statuses: pending_l1, pending_l2, update_requested, approved, rejected, withdrawn, cancelled (approved leave that was cancelled).
Payroll month

There is no month lock. Processing payroll only records the month as paid. Anything changed afterwards (leave, timesheets, attendance) is picked up by the next payroll. Loss of pay and retro adjustments are owned by the payroll team.
Payroll for a month can only be processed when every timesheet period in it is Approved (when timesheet approval is on).
Employee working days

The prototype uses company-wide weekly offs. The real build must use each employee’s own working days and shift (the per-employee schedule already in the latest code) for: late marks, hours targets, leave day counts, half days, the sandwich rule, calendars and comp off eligibility.
Email notifications for leave applications

Every time a leave application reaches an approval level, the approver(s) at that level get an email: Level 1 (reporting manager or the set person/team), the extra endorsement step (when it applies), and Level 2 (Admin / HR or the set person). Team approvers (Admin / HR) = every user with that role in the company.

Triggers: a new request is submitted (email to Level 1, or to the first level that isn’t skipped); a level approves and it moves on (email to the next level); an employee resubmits after "Ask for update" (email to Level 1 again). HR’s "Add leave" is approved straight away, so it sends none.
Covers every leave-type request: leave (including half days, per-event leave, maternity, LOP), leave cancellation and leave change requests, and comp off requests.

Email content (subject and body) will be shared separately by product. Build the sending and the triggers now with a template per trigger that uses placeholders: {approver_name}, {employee_name}, {employee_id}, {department}, {leave_type}, {from_date}, {to_date}, {days}, {day_type}, {reason}, {level}, {request_id}, {request_link} (deep link that opens the request in My team → Approvals or Payroll → Leave → Requests). Keep the wording in one editable place.

Send once per level per request (no duplicates on re-renders or retries); log each send (request, level, recipient, time, status). A failed email must never block the request. In-app notifications stay as they are.

3. Write docs/leave/plan.md: the screens to build or change, the rules to implement as tested functions, the data model and endpoints needed, how existing leave policy data maps to the new model, and the build order (settings → rules → ESS → approvers → Payroll → attendance/timesheet links).
